interpretations: Per rating, group all films by `rating`. Show the rating, the average `replacement_cost` over all of its films, the per-day price (AVG(`rental_rate`) / AVG(`rental_duration`)), and that per-day price divided by the unweighted mean of the five ratings' per-day prices. No rounding

Per-day price is the ratio of the two averages (AVG(`rental_rate`) / AVG(`rental_duration`)), not the average of each film's `rental_rate` / `rental_duration`. The comparison value is the simple mean of the 5 rating-level per-day prices, with each rating counted once

Same as 2, but the comparison value is a film-weighted overall per-day price: the overall AVG(`rental_rate`) / overall AVG(`rental_duration`) across all films. This reading ignores "each rating counted once."
Same as 2, but the comparison value is the mean of the per-film `rental_rate` / `rental_duration` values across all films

The average `replacement_cost` is taken over all films of each rating. Alternatively, it is taken only over films that have inventory copies, or weighted by the number of inventory copies (a stock-value average per copy)
Alternatively, the average `replacement_cost` is the stock value (SUM of `replacement_cost` over inventory copies) for each rating, rather than an average
The ratings considered are only those present in `film`. Alternatively, ratings are limited to films with rentals, or films appearing in `film_text`
"Do not round anything" means full-precision values with no ROUND or formatting. Alternatively, it means avoiding integer division, so values are cast to decimals or floats
The ratio column is the rating's per-day price divided by the mean (a relative index near 1). Alternatively, it is expressed as a percentage, or as the difference from the mean
The output may be ordered by `rating` alphabetically, by the ordinal audience restriction (G, PG, PG-13, R, NC-17), or by the ratio or per-day price. Alternatively, no ordering is specified

The per-day price might be read as the amount charged per rental day for a rating, i.e. `rental_rate` spread over `rental_duration` days. Alternatively, it is the `rental_rate` per day computed from actual rentals and payments (`payment`.`amount` divided by the days between `rental_date` and `return_date`)

Per-day price is read as the average of each film's `rental_rate` / `rental_duration` within the rating, rather than the ratio of the two averages. The comparison value is then the simple mean of those five rating-level averages
queries:
WITH r AS (
  SELECT rating,
         AVG(replacement_cost) AS avg_replacement_cost,
         AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) AS per_day_price
  FROM film
  GROUP BY rating
)
SELECT rating,
       avg_replacement_cost,
       per_day_price,
       per_day_price / (SELECT AVG(per_day_price) FROM r) AS ratio_to_mean
FROM r;
WITH r AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) AS per_day
  FROM film
  GROUP BY rating
)
SELECT rating
FROM r
WHERE per_day > (SELECT AVG(per_day) FROM r);
SELECT rating
FROM film
GROUP BY rating
HAVING AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) > (SELECT AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) FROM film);
SELECT title
FROM film
WHERE rental_rate / rental_duration > (SELECT AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) FROM film);
SELECT rating, AVG(replacement_cost) AS avg_replacement_cost FROM film GROUP BY rating
SELECT f.rating, SUM(f.replacement_cost) AS stock_value FROM inventory i JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating
